help.jira: Cloud: id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens. Data Center: your profile → Personal access tokens. A read-only account is enough.
help.github: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Fine-grained token, with read access to the Issues of the repositories involved.
help.gitlab: For issues of another project than the imported repository: a personal or project token with the read_api scope.
help.linear: Linear → Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys.
help.trello: trello.com/power-ups/admin: your Power-Up's API key, then a token generated from that page.
help.notion: notion.so/my-integrations: create an internal integration with “Read content”, then share your specification pages with it.
help.azure: Azure DevOps → User settings → Personal access tokens: a token with the Work Items (Read) scope.
help.youtrack: YouTrack → your profile → Account security → New token, with the YouTrack scope. A read-only account is enough.
help.openproject: OpenProject → My account → Access tokens → API: generate a key. Its account must see the projects involved.
help.redmine: Redmine → My account → API access key (Show). An administrator must enable the REST API under Administration → Settings → API.
help.asana: Asana → Settings → Apps → Developer apps (app.asana.com/0/my-apps): create a personal access token.
help.clickup: ClickUp → Settings → Apps → API Token: generate your personal token (starts with pk_).
help.shortcut: Shortcut → Settings → Your account → API Tokens: generate a token.
help.plane: Plane → Workspace settings → API tokens: add a token. Self-hosted: use your instance address instead of api.plane.so.
help.monday: monday.com → your avatar → Developers → My access tokens. Name the board columns that hold the status and, ideally, the approval date.
help.taiga: Taiga has no personal tokens: give an account that can read the project (a dedicated observer account is best). Self-hosted: your instance address, without /api/v1.
help.gitea: Gitea or Forgejo (Codeberg too) → Settings → Applications → Generate token, with read access to issues.
help.bugzilla: Bugzilla → Preferences → API Keys: generate a key. Read access to the products involved is enough.
help.mantis: MantisBT → My account → API tokens: create a token. The REST API must be enabled on the instance.

method.title: How Cairn decides
method.reference: The main branch is the reference: every merge request merged into it and every commit pushed directly.
method.tickets: Each delivery is matched with the tickets it cites, as they were approved; done tickets that never reach main are listed.
method.agents: AI agents are recognised by their Co-authored-by trailers, accounts and branch names, never by guessing.
method.deterministic: Rules only, no AI: the same history always gives the same result.
method.demo: Demo data: fictitious tickets and merges.
